root_cause: Text.__init__ (line 155), the plain setter (line 412) and Text.append (line 980) all run strip_control_codes() on incoming strings, but Text.append_tokens did not. A token such as 'long text ... control code \r\n' left a raw '\r' (zero cell width) in _text. Text.wrap/divide then computed line offsets that did not match the span positions, and the binary search in Text.divide indexed past line_ranges, raising IndexError: list index out of range when printed at width=40.
best_solution: In Text.append_tokens, add `content = strip_control_codes(content)` as the first line of the `for content, style in tokens:` loop, before append_text(content) and before the span offsets are computed from len(content). That makes append_tokens apply the same sanitisation invariant as every other way text enters a Text. The reasoning from the statement: 'exception in append_tokens' with no traceback means comparing append_tokens against its sibling append(), which strips control codes, and adding the missing step. strip_control_codes is already imported in rich/text.py.
acceptable_alternatives: Any fix that strips the STRIP_CONTROL_CODES set (\a \b \v \f \r) from each token before storing it and before computing span offsets, for example routing each token through self.append(content, style). Making divide/wrap tolerate control codes without stripping them would not pass, because the test asserts the exact output with '\r' removed.

our_outcome_summary: Failed under all four configs (v4, v6, v7, v8 kaggle_env_pass all false; pod runs 41-75 s, 13-24 calls). None of them found the control-code cause. They guessed at an 'exception' instead: v4 and v7 added `if tokens is None: return self` (v4 also widened the type hint to Optional, and v7 left a stray test_append_tokens.py in the repo root). v8 skipped tokens whose content is None. v6 deleted `self._length = offset`, which breaks len() after append_tokens and so makes things worse. The hidden test still raised IndexError in Text.divide (rich/text.py:1166), 1 failed / 107 passed.
generalizable_lesson: When a statement says only 'fix exception in function X' with no traceback, do not invent None or empty-input guards that the type hints already rule out. Diff X against its sibling entry points (the other constructors, setters and append/add variants that write the same internal state), find the normalisation or validation step they apply and X skips (sanitising, stripping, coercing, bounds checks), and add that step to X. A missing invariant on one entry path is the most common cause of a crash that shows up downstream. Build a quick repro with awkward but type-valid input (control characters, unicode, very long values) and run it through the downstream consumer (render/print/serialise) before choosing a fix.
